---
title: "MoE Expert Quantization"
description: "Reduce VRAM usage when training MoE model adapters by quantizing expert weights on load"
---

Transformers v5 changed MoE expert layers from `nn.Linear` to fused `nn.Parameter` (3D+ tensors).
This means `bitsandbytes` can no longer quantize them during model loading, resulting in all expert
weights being loaded in full bf16 precision and causing massive VRAM usage.

`quantize_moe_experts` solves this by quantizing expert weights during model loading.
It intercepts the weight loading process, quantizes each expert tensor on the fly, and
immediately frees the original bf16 tensor from VRAM. This dramatically reduces peak memory.
For example, GLM-4.7-Flash QLoRA drops from ~127GiB to ~23GiB reserved memory.

::: {.callout-tip}

For checkpoints that ship *already* quantized to NVFP4 (ModelOpt exports), see [NVFP4 MoE LoRA](nvfp4_lora.qmd) instead: the experts stay 4-bit-packed and the adapter can merge back into a plain NVFP4 model.

:::

## Usage

Enable expert quantization in your Axolotl config:

```yaml
quantize_moe_experts: true
```

This works with both 4-bit (QLoRA) and 8-bit (LoRA) quantization.

### Expert LoRA targeting

You can optionally apply LoRA adapters directly to expert weights using `lora_target_parameters`:

```yaml
lora_target_parameters:
  - mlp.experts.gate_up_proj
  - mlp.experts.down_proj
  # - mlp.gate.weight  # router
```

::: {.callout-note}
`lora_dropout` must be `0` when using `lora_target_parameters`.
:::

## Requirements

- Requires (`adapter: lora` and `load_in_8bit: true`) or (`adapter: qlora` and `load_in_4bit: true`)
- CUDA GPUs only (not tested with ROCm or other backends)
- FSDP2 compatible for distributed training

## Limitations

- `lora_target_linear` is not compatible with `quantize_moe_experts`. See [Expert LoRA targeting](#expert-lora-targeting) instead.
- With CPU-efficient loading disabled, the FSDP2 QLoRA loader needs the entire quantized model to fit on each GPU before sharding. Use the CPU-staged loader below to avoid this initial replica.
- Total model parameter count may display incorrectly (trainable param count is correct).
- FSDP LoRA (8-bit) may have a large initial VRAM spike at the first 1-2 steps, which then drops. QLoRA does not exhibit this.
- FSDP2 may use more VRAM per GPU than single GPU training due to not all layers being properly sharded across ranks.
- Model loading takes longer due to on-demand quantization, even on consecutive runs.
- DeepSpeed has not been tested.

## CPU-staged FSDP2 QLoRA loading

For models whose quantized weights do not fit on one GPU, enable:

```yaml
adapter: qlora
load_in_4bit: true
quantize_moe_experts: true
nf4_backend: bitsandbytes
fsdp_version: 2
fsdp_config:
  cpu_ram_efficient_loading: true
  state_dict_type: SHARDED_STATE_DICT
  auto_wrap_policy: TRANSFORMER_BASED_WRAP
  transformer_layer_cls_to_wrap: YourDecoderLayer
  reshard_after_forward: true
```

`qlora_sharded_model_loading` defaults to true for FSDP2 with `adapter: qlora`,
`load_in_4bit: true` and `cpu_ram_efficient_loading: true` when omitted or null.
An explicit false is preserved and requires disabling `cpu_ram_efficient_loading`.
For other configurations, the default remains false.

Replace `YourDecoderLayer` with the decoder class for your model. Rank zero reads
and quantizes the original floating-point checkpoint in bounded GPU chunks,
storing packed weights in CPU memory. Other ranks construct the model on the
meta device. Trainable adapters receive CPU storage before optimizer preparation so
Accelerate can map each adapter to its sharded parameter; frozen base weights remain
on meta on peer ranks. After FSDP wrapping, rank zero transfers individual parameter shards;
no rank needs a complete GPU replica during loading. Rank zero still needs CPU RAM
for the complete packed model and checkpoint conversion temporaries. A fused MoE
conversion can still require a complete floating-point expert tensor and its source
tensors on CPU. Quantization metadata
is replicated across ranks. Frozen base linear operations are checkpointed internally
so backward recomputes dense weights instead of retaining them for every layer. Training still needs enough GPU memory to gather and
execute an individual wrapped layer, including its dequantized weights. While shards are
distributed, rank zero also briefly holds one full packed tensor on its accelerator, bounded
by the largest quantized tensor; this peak is smaller than the wrapped-layer requirement
above.

`offload_params` controls FSDP parameter offloading after loading. This path supports
a single FSDP2 data-parallel mesh; DeepSpeed, tensor/context/expert parallelism,
DoRA, `modules_to_save` and value-dependent LoRA inits (pissa, olora, loftq, corda, eva) are unsupported.
olora remains available on the non-staged bitsandbytes loader with
`cpu_ram_efficient_loading: false` (the torchao backend is always staged); pissa and
loftq require an unquantized base.

A base model that is already quantized with bitsandbytes 4-bit (its `config.json`
carries a `quantization_config` with `quant_method: bitsandbytes` and `load_in_4bit`)
is adopted as-is: the checkpoint's packed weights and quantization state are staged
without requantizing, so `bnb_config_kwargs` that disagree with the checkpoint are
ignored (with a warning). The compute dtype must match the checkpoint's
`bnb_4bit_quant_storage` when that storage is a floating-point dtype. The torchao
backend and `quantize_moe_experts` still need an unquantized base checkpoint, and
`axolotl merge-lora` cannot merge an adapter back into a prequantized base: it streams
the base checkpoint and has no path that unpacks bitsandbytes components.

### LoRA init compatibility

| Init | Linear targets, non-staged 4-bit | Linear targets, CPU-staged | `lora_target_parameters` (fused experts) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default, `gaussian` | yes | yes | yes |
| `olora` | yes | rejected | rejected |
| `pissa`, `loftq` | rejected by PEFT (need an unquantized base) | rejected | rejected |
| `corda`, `eva` | not wired | rejected | rejected |

Value-dependent inits read and rewrite the base weight while the adapter is built.
Fused expert parameters have no `weight` attribute, so PEFT fails inside the init;
Axolotl rejects that combination at validation, before any weights load. Resuming an
adapter that was saved with a value-dependent init under CPU-staged loading is also
rejected: PEFT re-runs that init on load and the packed base cannot take its residual.
Convert such an adapter with PEFT's `path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` first.

### Long staging runs and progress

```yaml
ddp_timeout: 21600  # Seconds; six hours for rank-zero loading and metadata exchange.
```

NF4 staging creates a dedicated Gloo control group on every rank before loading.
Its timeout uses `AXOLOTL_NCCL_TIMEOUT` when set, otherwise `ddp_timeout`, otherwise
1800 seconds. This applies even if the default process group was initialized earlier.
Status and metadata broadcasts use CPU tensors on this group, so peers do not enter
NCCL bootstrap while rank zero is quantizing. This does not change an existing
training process group's timeout or the launcher's rendezvous timeout.

Logs identify checkpoint conversion, metadata preparation and broadcast, adapter initialization, FSDP wrapping, and shard distribution. Long phases
emit elapsed-time messages every minute; shard distribution also reports tensor counts.
An elapsed-time message indicates the phase has not finished, not proof that it is
making progress. Peer metadata is built on meta without copying CPU tensor data.

### Sharding and tensor shapes

The staged loader supports the one-dimensional FSDP2 data-parallel mesh with both
`reshard_after_forward: true` and `false`. Transformer-based and size-based wrapping
are supported, as is wrapping only the root module. Size-based wrapping keeps NF4
parametrization containers and expert adapter internals inside their owning module.
A root-only wrapper gathers the whole model for computation, so use decoder-layer
wrapping when the model does not fit on a single GPU.

Packed parameters stay uint8 under FSDP2 mixed precision: Axolotl stops FSDP2 casting
non-floating parameters to the policy's `param_dtype`, since converting packed bytes to
bf16 values corrupts the quantized base. They are sharded along their first storage
dimension, which need not align with expert or quantization block boundaries. FSDP gathers that storage before
NF4 reconstruction; logical weights retain the original dense or fused expert shape.
Uneven splits and empty adapter shards are supported. Quantization metadata remains
replicated. Full and sharded checkpoint formats preserve the global shapes.

Hybrid replicated/sharded meshes (`dp_replicate_size > 1`) are currently unsupported
and rejected. This restriction is separate from the `reshard_after_forward` setting.

### torchao NF4 alternative

Set `nf4_backend: torchao` to use torchao's `NF4Tensor` quantization for the frozen
base weights. It can also be used without FSDP on a single GPU. Linear weights and,
when enabled, fused expert weights are converted into bounded NF4Tensor chunks.
Packed storage is exposed through parametrizations so FSDP2 can shard it.

Torchao 0.18 is the pinned version; the loader also resolves 0.17's module path, where the NF4 implementation lived before the move.
Torchao uses NF4 codes with double-quantized scales, but its scale quantization is
different from bitsandbytes. Switching backends changes the quantized base weights.
The torchao path uses fixed 64-element weight blocks and 256-scale blocks, with
independent double quantization per chunk. It does not call bitsandbytes' int32
quantization kernels; bounded chunks also limit torchao's conversion temporaries.

The bitsandbytes path splits quantization and dequantization into block-aligned
chunks to avoid the native kernel's `2**31 - 1` element limit. It compresses the
complete scale vector once, preserving bitsandbytes' double-quantization semantics.
The final packed tensor and requested dequantized output still need to fit in memory.

### Resume and merge

Use `resume_from_checkpoint` with the same base checkpoint, NF4 backend, quantization
settings and adapter configuration. The base is reconstructed and sharded before
restoring the adapter and optimizer state. Both `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` and
`FULL_STATE_DICT` adapter checkpoints are supported. Optimizer restoration uses
Axolotl's pinned Accelerate loader.

Keep `nf4_backend` in the configuration passed to `axolotl merge-lora` and use
`merge_method: memory_efficient` (the default). The legacy CLI merge path is
rejected for staged NF4 adapters because it loads the original dense base. Merging
materializes the quantized base and applies the adapter delta, producing ordinary
floating-point weights. The memory-efficient merge path reproduces the selected
backend's quantization before adding the delta. Keep the training dtype and
`bnb_config_kwargs.llm_int8_skip_modules` unchanged for merging; both are part of
the quantized base definition.

Under staged loading, `llm_int8_skip_modules` entries match in one of three ways:

- A plain name or dotted path matches by name: `lm_head` excludes that module
  wherever it appears, `model.layers.0.mlp` excludes that subtree, and `proj`
  excludes only a module named exactly `proj`, not `q_proj`.
- A leading or trailing dot requests a plain substring match against the full
  parameter path: `_proj.` excludes every `*_proj` weight.
- Regex metacharacters request a regular-expression search over the full
  parameter path: `layers\.[0-3]\.` excludes the first four layers.

`lm_head` and `embed_out` are always excluded.

Because these rules differ from Transformers' `modules_to_not_convert`, a key that
worked under plain QLoRA can match nothing here. At the end of staging the loader
logs, for every exclusion entry, its matching tier and how many quantization
candidates it excluded, and warns for each `llm_int8_skip_modules` entry that
excluded none; check that warning before assuming a module stayed unquantized.

## Implementation details

The quantization is applied by patching transformers to intercept weight loading.
When a 3D+ CUDA tensor with "expert" in its name is detected:

- **4-bit mode:** Uses bitsandbytes NF4 parametrization (configurable via `bnb_4bit_quant_type`).
- **8-bit mode:** Uses a custom row-wise int8 parametrization with bitsandbytes dequantization.

The original bf16 tensor is freed immediately after quantization. Multiple sub-patches are applied to
transformers, PEFT and accelerate FSDP2 to support these parametrized expert modules.

For full implementation details, see [PR #3439](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/pull/3439).
